subject: Sunrise Bio: hosted API — data closure & geographic handling Q&A
messages:

Cc: Security Team <security@sunrisebio.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs on data closure, backups & region-specific purges

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the earlier checklist. We have a few follow-ups for the hosted API:

1) If a tenant requests an account deletion, what exact steps does Redwood take to remove their data from active stores, cache (including KV and prefix caches), and backups? Please provide expected wall-clock timelines for each stage.
2) Are persistent backups / snapshots retained outside of the region where the tenant ran workloads? We need to confirm whether backups are geo-replicated and where they live.
3) For long-running asynchronous jobs (ingestion/embedding pipelines) that reference customer data, how is deletion enforced if those jobs are mid-flight?
4) Do you provide deletion attestations and an audit trail we can pull for compliance?

We're under a compressed timeline for our internal privacy review this week. If possible, a short, numbered response would help us put answers into the questionnaire matrix.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Information Security
Sunrise Bio

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@sunrisebio.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on data closure, backups & region-specific purges

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are targeted to the hosted API configuration (no Private/Dedicated changes). I'll attach a concise response pdf for your packet (Sunrise_Security_Responses_v1.pdf) and a deletion-flow diagram.

1) Account deletion steps & timelines (hosted API):
   - Active stores (primary object & metadata stores): triggered immediately when deletion is requested; logical deletions occur within minutes and are propagated to dependent services in under 1 hour.
   - KV / prefix caches: caches are ephemeral by design; prefix / KV caches are invalidated within 60 seconds after persistent store deletion. Cache entries are never used as canonical stores and are evicted on a rolling basis.
   - Model runtime memory / KV-cache snapshots: per-instance in-memory KV is cleared on session termination. If a long-lived session exists, we proactively terminate sessions associated with a deleted tenant within 15 minutes of deletion confirmation.
   - Backups & snapshots: managed snapshots are retained for durability; snapshot lifecycle begins at creation and is subject to deletion windows below (Backups: 30/90 window).

   Expected wall-clock summary: logical deletion of primary data: minutes (<=60m); cache invalidation: <=60s; active session termination: <=15m; snapshot lifecycle start-to-deletion: see backups section.

2) Backups, geo-replication & geography:
   - By default (hosted API standard tier), snapshots are stored in the region where the tenant's primary compute/storage lives and are not automatically geo-replicated to other regions.
   - For customers with specific geo-replication requirements (enterprise / contractual add-on), we provide explicit replication to a second region; this is only enabled when contractually requested.
   - Cross-region emergency replication (for disaster recovery) is controlled by the platform team and only enabled for account classes that require it; such replication is documented in the customer's security addendum.

3) In-flight work and deletion enforcement:
   - Long-running jobs reference input data via pointers to primary storage. When deletion is requested, new work is blocked and running jobs are signalled to fail-fast; they are instrumented to drop references to deleted objects within the next checkpoint cycle (typically within 5–20 minutes depending on job type).
   - For asynchronous pipelines that must complete for operational reasons, customers can request a controlled erasure window (we provide a short-lived retention hold and explicit attribution for audit). If you require immediate stop-and-erase, we terminate the job and orphaned intermediate artifacts are swept by the normal erasure pipeline.

4) Deletion attestations & audit trail:
   - We produce a machine-readable deletion attestation (PDF + structured JSON) that lists objects removed, deletion timestamps, and the actor (API key or support engineer) that triggered the event.
   - Audit logs are retained per our standard audit retention policy (90 days for hosted audit logging; extended retention available under enterprise add-on). Audit logs include API calls, job lifecycle events, and snapshot deletions.

Extra detail on backup lifecycle (requested because it's often a follow-up):
   - Snapshots are subject to tiered retention: auto-snapshots (30 days); customer-requested compliance snapshots (90 days by default unless a different term is contracted).
   - Snapshot deletion is performed in two phases: logical deletion (marked and made inaccessible) and physical deletion (blocks zeroed and storage reclaimed). Physical reclamation windows vary by underlying provider; we expect physical reclamation within 30–90 days after logical deletion depending on provider object-store behavior. We include the logical deletion timestamp in the attestation.

Evidence & attachments: the attached PDF includes the same answers plus a simple flowchart (data-deletion-flowchart.png) showing where attestations and audit records are produced.

If useful, I can create a short appendix that maps your questionnaire fields directly to our answers.

Thanks — Lukas

Elena — looping in a quick confirmation from ops:

- The physical reclamation window for hosted API snapshots does not exceed 120 days in any supported cloud region. The typical range is 30–90 days, but in rare cases (third-party provider object-store replication & legal hold interactions) we have seen final reclamation take up to 120 days; we will note that as the contractual maximum for hosted customers.

- I've attached a sanitized sample attestation in the PDF (Sunrise_Security_Responses_v1.pdf, page 4). If you need the JSON schema rather than the human-readable PDF, reply and we will provide the machine-readable example under an NDA if you prefer.

Next steps: if you accept the 120-day contractual max, we can produce a short addendum clause and provide the machine-readable attestation schema. Otherwise, tell us the maximum you need and we will route the request to legal/ops for feasibility.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
